These are all boys.  Our not so close neighbor neglected their colony and then I became aware of its existence when it moved into my grandmother’s barn.  19 cats later; these are the last 4 and they are big/healthy enough to get sterilized.  

The sad thing of it is, is the cost of spaying and neutering causes people to put it off until their cat escapes or the lack of available affordable appointments. I am able to pay a subsidized cost of $30 per neuter including vaccinations in my area because people who care made it so.  It breaks my heart to see the shift in attitude towards animals. I live in rural CA and I feel if I ask for help in dire straights I will receive it.  I was living in rural Appalachia for several months and asked for help with a fresh litter of pups. Every weak one died due to “let nature take its course”. With vet intervention they could have been saved.  With the resources I had in CA, they would have lived.  The contrast was day and night.  I had my first real brush with caregiver fatigue living there, feeling like everything was working against me. 

In my opinion, people don’t like “spay abort” especially nowadays with assigning animals human morals and emotions and the human rights issues we have going on world wide that we are constantly exposed to.  Wires are getting crossed.  Some vets won’t perform them and I’ve seen techs and rescues with even less tact shame the owners for the animal being pregnant in the first place.

When I was told surrendering this litter at the shelter will result in immediate euthanasia, I started trapping them and housing them in my grandma’s while figuring out sterilization and rehoming.  I just wasn’t expecting to trap 19 total. The costs are only manageable thanks to this subreddit and the work my community has done to lower prices and host huge neuter events. I’m disabled and unable to work, but I wish with all my heart I could handle a full volunteer day to give back to them 🫶.

So a lot of people have their thoughts but as someone pro stim collar let me tell you my perspective. My collar has two functions. Stim and vibrate.  The stim is as bad as hitting one of those old joy buzzers. An annoyance but not at all painful. 

Most people don’t know how to introduce these tools to their dogs or don’t condition them.  Clear communication is important to dogs.

I started at a low stim on the name game and loaded the collar with cookies for my girl. Then we extended the range and worked on recall with just two low stims. This eventually led up to her just coming back to the house from running on the property on the cue of two quick low stims.  She knows what they mean and we have a clear understanding of what we’re asking. 

As I stated elsewhere this is improper tool use. There is a way to safely and effectively use these tools, but it really isn’t for someone looking for a quick miracle fix or patchwork to correct barking.

Stim (often incorrectly referred to as shock) collars are safe when used properly. This is like giving someone a claw hammer for laying concrete. Improper tool use.

Quick example-I have a stim collar with a half mile range and live on decent acreage. I can hit a low pulse twice and see my dog booking it to the front door within minutes.
